hyps.why: If edge 1 is none, node 2 gets input only through edge 2, so a conv on edge 2->3 has less signal to process and helps less.
With edge 0 removed, node 1 has no input, so a conv on edge 1->3 does nothing useful.
Replacing none with a skip adds a gradient-friendly direct path, which is a larger gain than replacing an already useful op.
Removing a 3x3 conv costs more accuracy than removing a pool or skip.
Deleting a 3x3 conv from the first edge is much more damaging than deleting a weak op.
Replacing none with a conv on the direct edge gains more than replacing skip or pool.
Node 1 has no input when edge 0 is none, so a conv on edge 1->2 has nothing to process.
Removing a 3x3 conv on edge 1 loses more than removing a weak op.
Adding a conv where there was none gains more than swapping one non-none op for another.
With edge 1 removed, node 2 carries less useful signal, so a skip on edge 2->3 adds little.
